content: Both sides capture important moral stakes: your brother’s focus on saving lives reflects a strong utilitarian commitment to maximizing collective well-being, while your flatmate’s insistence on personal freedom speaks to a deep respect for bodily autonomy and individual self‑determination. The policy change embodies a real clash of values—between the desire to increase life‑saving donations and the right to decide what becomes of one’s own body—rather than a simple case of one view being “wrong.”
